- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is flat or rising, aggressively lower forecast to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling after peak), model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast by 1–3% per day of lag.  
- If sentiment history includes a recent 1.00 (strong bullish signal), model often overreacts — cap forecast at 10–15% above prior peak.  
- If forecast is >85% of prior 30-day average and true outcome is below 75%, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence bias.
